Technicals:
The index barely moved — Nifty ‑0.10% to 24,055.80 — and that is the most misleading number on the page. Underneath, the share of Nifty 500 stocks above their 20‑day average fell from
41% to 33%
in a single session.
📈
Domestic:
Damage was concentrated, not broad.
Nifty Bank ‑1.06%
and
Midcap 100 ‑1.39%
, with Shriram Finance ‑4.58% and Maruti ‑4.41% among the heaviest large-cap losers. IT was the only sector adding participation.
🌍
Global:
US–Iran hostilities resumed after a month of calm. US forces struck Larak Island, Iran hit targets in the UAE and Jordan, and a supertanker caught fire on mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent rose 0.87% to $91.28
, a second straight day higher.
💰
Flows:
Foreign investors
flipped to buyers
, +₹1,143.38 Cr after yesterday's ₹7,985.88 Cr sale. Domestic institutions added ₹1,846.94 Cr. Read it with care — expiry day distorts a single session's flow.
⚡
Event:
Weekly expiry settled at
24,055.80
, inside the 24,000–24,200 band this report projected yesterday. The Adani names rebounded, which was the specific test we set for whether Monday's collapse was mechanical.

The market has been calmer than on all but about 40 of the last 250 days. Calm scores high here, but the average daily range has not widened even as oil climbs and banks fall — the quiet is in the index, not in the stocks underneath it.
Read the composition, not the number.
The score rose

37.9

§3
What's Unusual Today
Nifty IT participation jumped 60 points in five sessions
1 of 24
The largest single-sector rotation this report has recorded. The share of IT stocks above their 20-day average went from a small minority to a clear majority inside a week. IT was also the only sector to gain participation today while every other one lost it.
Vardhman Textiles +5.29% on 36.5× normal volume
The most extreme volume reading in the entire universe by a wide margin — more than double the next highest. A move this size on that much volume is a crowd arriving in one session, not a drift.
Engineers India +6.94% on 15.7× volume
Second-heaviest volume expansion of the day, and the top gainer among construction names.
Caplin Point +7.7% on 11.2× volume
The day's largest gain, on the third-heaviest volume — and notable because healthcare was otherwise the day's second-worst sector at ‑1.60%.
Nifty ATR still 0.73% of price
41 of 250
The average daily range has not widened at all, through an oil shock, a bank selloff and an expiry. Realised volatility remains near the calm end of 250 sessions while the market's internals deteriorate — a divergence worth watching rather than trusting.
Both FII and DII bought on the same session
28 of 36
Foreign +₹1,143.38 Cr and domestic +₹1,846.94 Cr. After four sessions of the two pulling in opposite directions, they agreed today — though expiry-day mechanics make one session a weak signal.
Welspun Corp +6.8%, and in both momentum tables
A name entering momentum today that is also already in a confirmed weekly trend. Only two stocks qualify for both.
KEI Industries ‑6.83%, Polycab ‑5.82%
The two largest cable and wire names fell together and led the losers, a sector-specific move rather than part of the broad decline.
Graphite India +4.32% on 5.8× volume
Part of a scattered bid in capital goods that ran counter to the day's direction.
Nifty 500 advance/decline at 0.64
86 of 246
Better than yesterday's 0.56 but still two fallers for every three risers — on a day the index closed almost unchanged. The flat headline hides three consecutive sessions of negative breadth.
Ranked by how unusual each reading is against its own history, not by which number is largest. Window lengths are in the pack; ranks shown as position out of window.

§4
Macro & Policy Dashboard
US–Iran hostilities resume
ESCALATION
1 Sep 2026 · Strait of Hormuz
US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island; Iran responded with attacks on the UAE and Jordan.
A supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz, per Iranian state media.
This ends roughly a month of relative calm and revives the risk of disruption to a corridor carrying a large share of seaborne crude.
Trader implication:
this is now a live, unscheduled variable. There is no release date to position around, which is precisely what makes it hard to hedge.
Brent above $91
SECOND DAY UP
1 Sep 2026 · +0.87% to $91.28
Up from $90.69 yesterday and $88.29 on Friday — roughly
3.4% in two sessions
.
India imports the overwhelming majority of its crude. Every dollar widens the trade deficit and pressures the rupee.
Direct margin pressure for paints, tyres, aviation, chemicals and logistics; a tailwind only for upstream producers.
Trader implication:
oil has now outweighed a 7.8% GDP print two sessions running. Watch it before anything domestic.
Weekly expiry settled
AS PROJECTED
Tue 1 Sep · Nifty weekly options
Settled at
24,055.80
, inside the 24,000–24,200 band yesterday's report gave the pin scenario at ~55%.
Max pain was 24,100; the close came 44 points below it — near the pin rather than exactly on it.
The 24,000 put floor was tested intraday for a second straight session (low 23,952.55) and held into the close.
Trader implication:
the next weekly expiry is Tuesday 8 September, and the Sensex weekly settles Thursday 3 September on the BSE.

A/D D-1
is the advance/decline for yesterday.
%>20D D-1
is the percentage of stocks in that index trading above their 20-day SMA, yesterday.
A/D Today
tells you how the index performed today — what the advance-to-decline ratio was.
%>20D SMA
tells you what percentage of stocks in that universe is trading above its 20-day simple moving average. Watch how the A/D ratio moved from last week to today, and how %>20D SMA moved over the same stretch — those two shaded pairs are the comparison this table exists for.
A rising index with
increasing advances and more stocks above the 20D SMA
means broader participation in the rally. A rising index on
very narrow participation
can instead mean index management, indecision, or only a few sectors doing the work while the rest of the market goes nowhere.
The single most important number in this report:
the share of Nifty 500 stocks above their 20-day average fell from 41% to 33% while the index moved 0.10%
. Yesterday the same measure held flat as breadth collapsed; today it broke. Three sessions of negative advance/decline have now worked their way into the trend positions.
Snapshots: 2026-09-01 · 2026-08-31 · 2026-08-28 · 2026-08-25. All percentages are whole numbers. The 5-day participation change and the full SMA ladder (20/50/100/200) are carried in the data pack and read in §8 rather than shown here.

§8
Sector Rotation
Rotating in
Information Technology
— participation up an extraordinary
60 points
in five sessions, the largest rotation this report has recorded. IT rose 0.98% today while thirteen of fourteen sectors fell, and is up 2.36% on the week.
Private Banks and Pharma
— each up 10 points of participation over the week, though both fell today. Improving from a low base rather than leading.
Rotating out
Auto
— participation down
47 points
in five sessions, the worst on the board, and ‑2.48% on the week. Maruti fell 4.41% today. This was already deteriorating yesterday and accelerated.
Realty
— down 40 points, ‑2.89% on the week, ‑1.42% today. Second consecutive session as one of the worst.
Media
— down 30 points and ‑3.02% on the week, extending a month-long decline with no base forming.
Oil & Gas
— down 26 points despite rising crude, which is the counter-intuitive one: higher oil hurts refiners and marketers more than it helps producers in this index.
Midcaps broadly
— Midcap 100 and Next 50 both shed 22 points of participation. The broader market is where the selling actually landed.
Yesterday's defensive rotation has narrowed to a single sector.
On Monday, hospitals, pharma, healthcare and banks were all gaining participation. Today only IT is — and every other sector, including the defensives that led yesterday, lost ground. A rotation that narrows this fast is usually not a rotation; it is the market retreating to one hiding place.

Foreign investors flipped to buyers, and the temptation is to read too much into it.
After Monday's ₹7,985.88 Cr sale — the heaviest in the retained window — they bought ₹1,143.38 Cr today, ranking a merely ordinary 28th of 36 sessions. Domestic institutions added ₹1,846.94 Cr, modest by their own August standard. Two things argue for caution. First, this was expiry day, when settlement mechanics move cash-market prints in ways that say little about conviction. Second, the week as a whole still shows foreign investors
selling ₹11,677 Cr
against domestic buying of ₹23,022 Cr. One session does not reverse that. What it does do is remove the extreme: yesterday the flow component of the regime score was near its floor, today it is mid-range, and that alone lifted the composite.

The one thing to carry into tomorrow.
The index closed almost exactly where it opened the week, and that flat line is hiding a market that is quietly getting narrower — participation down from 41% to 33% in a session, thirteen of fourteen sectors losing ground, and a derivatives book that has moved from balanced to distinctly ceiling-heavy. Two of yesterday's calls held, which is worth something. But nothing in today's data argues that the deterioration underneath has stopped, and oil is still climbing.
Most readers open at the index level and stop there — which is the habit that makes a narrow market look healthy.
1
Start with participation, not the index
Open §7. Which direction is the number of stocks above their 20-day average moving? That is the market’s direction of travel, not the index close.
2
Then check the index against it
If the Nifty rose but fewer stocks are above their 20-day average than yesterday, participation is falling inside a rising index. That divergence is the most important thing on the page.
3
Read sector leadership across timeframes
In §6b, compare each sector’s 1-day move against its 1-week and 1-month bars. A sector strong on the day but weak on the month is a bounce. A sector strong on all three is a trend.
4
Cross-check each sector’s move against its own breadth
A sector that rose today but whose participation column is falling has a narrow move — a few stocks doing the work. §6b row next to §7 row is the comparison.
5
Go straight to the flagged sectors
The pack has already joined breadth to the scanners for you. Read §7’s notable flags and §9’s scanner names together — that join is already done.
6
Ask whether the money agrees with the positioning
Compare §11 (what institutions bought and sold) with §13 (where the derivatives positioning sits). Conviction shows when both point the same way.
